subsystems.name: Positioning stage
subsystems.role: moves the tool relative to the workpiece with accuracy better than an atom's width, and holds it there.

subsystems.name: Probe tip and tool
subsystems.role: the working 'hand' — an atomically sharp apex that picks up, moves and chemically bonds molecular fragments.
parts: functionalised apex (a single atom or small cluster)

subsystems.name: Feedstock delivery
subsystems.role: brings molecular building blocks to the tip cleanly and in the right order.

subsystems.name: Sensing and feedback
subsystems.role: reads what just happened at the surface and corrects the next move.

subsystems.name: Synthesis planning
subsystems.role: works out which reactions and moves build a target structure, atom by atom.

subsystems.name: Parallel tip arrays
subsystems.role: many tips working at once, because one tip is far too slow to make anything useful.

buildSteps.title: Design the structure and its route
buildSteps.detail: Choose a target — say a stiff covalent lattice — then use simulation to break it into molecular building blocks and a sequence of bond-forming steps, as a chemical route rather than a blueprint.

buildSteps.title: Make atomically sharp tips
buildSteps.detail: Etch or field-evaporate metal or silicon to a radius near 1 nanometre, then attach a chosen atom or small cluster to the apex so it performs one specific reaction.

buildSteps.title: Build the positioning environment
buildSteps.detail: Combine piezoelectric stages, interferometer metrology, ultra-high vacuum and cryogenic cooling so the tip and surface stay fixed to within about 0.01 nanometres for hours.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate a single bond
buildSteps.detail: Use the tip to pick up one molecular fragment and press it onto another, forming a covalent bond on demand. This has been done for a few surface reactions (for example hydrogen on silicon) but not yet as general carbon–carbon mechanosynthesis.

buildSteps.title: Chain steps into a sequence
buildSteps.detail: Repeat place-bond-check thousands of times without contaminating the surface, adding imaging between steps so mistakes are found and reversed rather than built in.

buildSteps.title: Scale out with parallel arrays
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate thousands of independently driven cantilevers on one chip, each running the same sequence over its own patch of substrate, to turn an experiment into a production method.

buildSteps.title: Build a macroscale part
buildSteps.detail: Grow the structure layer by layer into a component big enough to hold and test — a task that would take an array working for a very long time, which is why the economics are unresolved.

buildSteps.title: Characterise and integrate
buildSteps.detail: Measure strength, stiffness and defects, then bond the part to conventional hardware. Only then can any claim of extreme strength-to-weight ratio be checked rather than assumed.

prerequisites.why: researchers have dragged and placed individual atoms and written patterns with them since the late 1980s, proving the concept but not the factory.
tip-induced hydrogen removal on silicon works and is used in research lithography, but forming arbitrary covalent bonds with a tip is not yet routine.

prerequisites.tech: Sub-nanometre positioning and metrology at speed
prerequisites.why: today's instruments are precise but slow, and drift over minutes; production needs precision held over hours.
simulations can propose tip reactions but are not yet reliable enough to predict outcomes without experiment.
large cantilever arrays exist for data storage and microscopy research, but not with the individual chemical control needed here.

prerequisites.tech: Cleanliness and error correction at scale
prerequisites.why: a single stray molecule ruins a structure, and no one has shown how to find and fix errors fast enough to matter.

pathway.milestone: single-atom placement and tip-induced surface chemistry in ultra-high vacuum
pathway.unlocks: tools and know-how for controlled bond making.

pathway.milestone: a demonstrated, repeatable mechanosynthetic reaction sequence forming a small well-defined molecule
pathway.unlocks: evidence that atom-by-atom construction is chemistry, not just manipulation.

pathway.milestone: parallel tip arrays producing simple atomically precise building blocks at useful rates
pathway.unlocks: realistic cost estimates and the first niche materials.

pathway.milestone: a general-purpose assembler building macroscale parts
pathway.unlocks: materials with exceptional stiffness and strength — if speed, cleanliness and repair can all be solved, which remains speculative.
